title: Is it worth switching to Claude for browser game development?
author: multiversecitizen
selftext:
Hey everyone! I’ve recently leaned toward browser-based game development, as it’s easier to test different ideas quickly. I also learned that there’s a better chance of actually gaining traction on platforms like CrazyGames and Poki compared to mobile app stores. (I know Steam gives you that chance too, but I don’t think I’m ready or have the time for a bigger game concept just yet.)

I’m currently using Antigravity, and while Gemini’s models are okay, the results aren't always satisfying and are often full of bugs. I know Claude models are supposed to be way better, but I’m not sure if it makes that much of a difference for basic browser games.

So, I’m curious about your opinions. Which models, workflows, and agent skills do you use for browser games? Is it worth ditching Gemini and moving to a potentially more expensive model? Is Claude Pro tier enough for this kind of development?

I’ve been reading your stories and comments, and they've been super inspiring, so thanks in advance for your answers!

comments.author: bingewavecinema
comments.body:
Yes! Much easier to build and test. Also for monetization, CrazyGames/Poki is advertisign based, [gltich.fun](http://gltich.fun) is subscritpion and premium based, [itch.io](http://itch.io) is donation based. Distributeon what aligns with you.

Gemini models are garbage, use codex or claude and threejs.

replies.author: multiversecitizen
replies.body: Thanks! Which platform do you suggest for beginners? Which one has the most potential for an income?

comments.author: re-skob
comments.body: Use Open AI codex - they're way more generous with tokens/usage, Codex is a really well put together app, and GPT 5.5 is great with 5.6 coming out in the next few weeks and is supposedly going to be competitive with Fable.

replies.author: multiversecitizen
replies.body: Which subscription tier do you recommend?

replies.author: re-skob
replies.body: Start with the $20 plan and scale up as you need it

replies.author: datNovazGG
replies.body: Furthermore Open AI allows for you to use other agent harnesses than Codex whereas with claude models you're only allowed (for subscriptions that is) to use Claude code or Claude apps.

comments.author: rapkannibale
comments.body: Most LLMs are pretty good at developing web based apps but not very good at actually making a game fun. So yes given you prompt it properly and provide good game design ideas (or brainstorm it with AI first) it will be very capable

replies.author: multiversecitizen
replies.body: How do you do that? You start with an idea and iterate it with AI or just ask it to come with new ideas?

replies.author: rapkannibale
replies.body: Yeah just do something like “You are a senior game designer. Your task is to help me brainstorm and idea for a game that….” And then give it as much context for the game you want the target audience, the platform etc”

comments.author: dazreil
comments.body: Been using codex, I been working on the mechanics first before anything else, trying to make is fun. So far it’s light years ahead of using just plain old ChatGPT. Any bugs I’ve picked up are usually from me not explaining the mechanics well enough or from iterating on an iteration.

replies.author: multiversecitizen
replies.body: Thanks! Which tier do you use and is it enough?

comments.author: donkeykong917
comments.body:
Claude fable can do alot of this be shot three.js games. As I had token to spare. I decided to make alot of sloppy games using fable. https://simplegame.au/

Pretty much zero effort put in but once you get going you can start doing fine-tuning when you have struck gold with an idea.

Games have alot to do with assets and textures, sfx wnd music. That will marry it up and polish it nicely. That will probably take most of the time to either. Polishing for release.

replies.author: multiversecitizen
replies.body: That’s neat! I tried a couple of games and they look nice! Are these all one-shots or you polished them? Also what do you use for audio-visual asset generation?

replies.author: donkeykong917
replies.body:
Claude fable did the polish and added sfx/visuals. I just said polish each game after. Opus does an ok job too after I ran out.

But in all seriousness, if you get make one game, you can slowly polish element or ask it for suggestions for improvement and then choose.
